chapter_title: The Rise of Open-Weights Models and Local Deployment

questions.question: What is the approximate base VRAM requirement for running a 27B parameter model at 4-bit quantization?
questions.explanation: The calculation is (27 billion parameters * 4 bits) / 8 = 13.5 gigabytes.

questions.question: True or False: Local deployment of large language models eliminates per-token inference costs.
questions.explanation: Local execution runs on your own hardware, removing the need to pay for cloud API usage.
questions.flashcard_front: Does local deployment eliminate per-token costs?
questions.flashcard_explanation: Local models run on your own hardware, removing cloud API fees.

questions.question: Why is quantization considered a 'necessary technique' for local LLM deployment?
questions.answer: It reduces the memory footprint of large models, enabling them to fit into the limited VRAM/RAM of consumer-grade hardware.
questions.explanation: Without quantization, the memory requirements for high-parameter models would exceed the capacity of most consumer workstations.
questions.flashcard_front: Why is quantization necessary for local LLMs?
questions.flashcard_back: Reduces memory footprint to fit on consumer hardware.
questions.flashcard_explanation: Quantization compresses model weights, allowing large models to run on limited VRAM.
